**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the merge command to the validated head SHA**

If another actor pushes between this live-state read and the subsequent merge, a bare `gh pr merge` can merge the new head even though only the previous SHA passed `merge-ready`. The inspected `gh pr merge --help` documents `--match-head-commit SHA` as “Commit SHA that the pull request head must match to allow merge”; require that flag with the validated SHA and rerun the gate on a mismatch rather than relying on “immediately before” ordering.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the live base against the delivery record**

When the PR is retargeted or its base branch advances after `record-delivery` without changing the PR head, this still treats the delivery as current because `deliveryCurrent` compares only review IDs and the merge evidence contains no live base SHA. Consequently, fresh green checks and reviewer evidence can produce `ready` while the acceptance criteria and disposition were evaluated against the record's older `baseSha`; pass the live base in the evidence and block or re-record when it differs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require every recorded check in the live evidence**

When the live-check query returns an empty or incomplete list—for example while a required check is being rerun—this loop sees no non-success conclusion and the gate can return `ready`; it also accepts an unrelated successful check in place of the delivery record's named required check. Since the current delivery already exposes `requiredChecks`, compare those names against the live evidence and block any missing check rather than treating absence as success.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject reviewer evidence without an identity**

If reviewer normalization produces an entry with no login—for example `{ "terminal": true, "lgtm": true }` after receiving a null or deleted actor—the nonempty array suppresses `no-automated-review`, and the entry adds no blocking reason because `name` is never validated. The gate therefore returns `ready` with no attributable automated reviewer; reject entries whose normalized reviewer name is empty before counting them as review evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind merge readiness to the live contract digest**

If the approved ticket or acceptance criteria are edited after `record-delivery` without changing the PR head, this gate can still return `ready`: the live evidence carries no `contractDigest`, and `deliveryStatus` considers the stored record current based only on review activity. The earlier resume-time comparison does not protect against contract changes between recording and merging, so require the freshly computed contract digest here and block or re-record when it differs from the delivery record.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the validated PR to gh pr merge**

When the skill is run from a checkout whose current branch belongs to a different PR, this command does not necessarily merge the PR named by the user and checked by `merge-ready`. The inspected `gh pr merge --help` states, “Without an argument, the pull request that belongs to the current branch is selected”; `--match-head-commit` usually turns this into a failure, but two PRs can share a head commit and then the wrong PR can be merged. Pass the validated PR number or URL as the positional argument.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block merging while a fix round is active**

After a mergeable delivery is recorded, a human can run `waive-fix-budget`, which deliberately makes that delivery nonterminal for `claim-fix-round`; a fixer can then claim the same head while `delivery.current` and its mergeable classification remain unchanged. Because this gate never checks `fixRoundForHead` or an abandoned fix claim, it still returns `ready` while the claimed fixer is preparing unpublished changes, allowing the PR to merge out from under the active round. Treat any open or abandoned fix claim as blocking and require a new delivery record after the round completes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not bypass the gate when a configured reviewer is absent**

When a configured reviewer has not produced any current-head activity, the evidence can have an empty `reviewers` array and `merge-ready` correctly returns `blocked` with `no-automated-review`; this sentence nevertheless tells the agent to merge on the user's explicit request, which is already the prerequisite for every agent merge. That overrides the preceding “on `blocked`, do not merge” rule and recreates the pending-review race this gate is intended to prevent; the exception must distinguish a repository with no configured reviewers from a configured reviewer that is merely unobserved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require evidence for every configured reviewer**

When multiple automated reviewers are configured and the caller accidentally omits one, any nonempty subset of terminal reviewers with LGTM passes this test and can make the gate return `ready`; for example, completed Codex evidence allows merging while a configured Copilot review is still missing or pending. The gate needs an expected reviewer set, derived from configuration or supplied separately and validated, so omissions are represented as blockers rather than silently disappearing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
